descriptionChirho: A feminine noun denoting a trembling or shuddering, and by metonymy the object that causes such terror; an object of horror or dread. Found with both spellings זְוָעָה and the transposed form זַעֲוָה. Used exclusively in prophetic contexts of divine judgment, where nations or peoples are made 'an object of horror' to surrounding kingdoms: Isa 28:19 'it will be sheer terror to understand the message'; Jer 15:4; 24:9; 29:18; 34:17 nations given as לְזוָֹעָה 'for a horror / an object of trembling' among the kingdoms of the earth; 2 Chr 29:8 Israel itself becoming 'an object of horror.' All occurrences (including Ketiv/Qere variants) express a single semantic concept of terror-inducing dread or the state of being an object of horrified trembling.
